Farmers around the world navigate shifti: Farmers around the world navigate shifting temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, water shortages, extreme weather, and declining soil health. These pressures make it difficult to choose crop rotations that protect fields, conserve water, and support long-term resilience. Your challenge is to create a decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth observations along with local soil information, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to help farmers explore rotation strategies that could strengthen soil health and adapt their farms to changing conditions.
Farmers around the world are making rota: Farmers around the world are making rotation decisions under conditions that no longer behave as they used to. Temperatures are shifting, rainfall is less predictable, and water shortages, erosion, nutrient depletion and extreme weather add uncertainty every season. Soil health is declining across many regions.
Choosing which crops to add to a rotatio: Choosing which crops to add to a rotation has become hard because no crop is good everywhere. A crop that builds soil in one place may use too much water in another, bring in disease, conflict with local markets, or fall outside the expected growing season.
We developed a web-based decision-suppor: We developed a web-based decision-support tool that helps farmers plan crop rotations for a changing climate. It combines NASA Earth observations (such as POWER weather, GPM IMERG rainfall, SMAP soil moisture, HLS v2.0 imagery and NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections etc.) with other sources like ESA Sentinel-1 radar, the USDA Cropland Data Layer and USDA soil surveys and more.
Our tool enables farmers to explore real: Our tool enables farmers to explore real-time and historical metrics of each field. Machine-learning and statistical models provide real-time analysis of each field’s health and several rotation strategies for consideration.
An SI assistant makes our tool customisa: An SI assistant makes our tool customisable for user’s priorities and constraints and interpretable for people with any level of technical or geospatial experience, explaining each strategy’s benefits, evidence, gaps and risks. It supports farmers’ judgment and local expertise, not replaces them.
We are a five-frog team from Ukraine wit: We are a five-frog team from Ukraine with experience in building high-load production systems, powered with large scale data and machine learning pipelines. We’ve competed in several hackathons, so we know how to scope tightly, split work cleanly and ship a working demo under pressure. Our strength is turning large, messy datasets into tools people can actually use. We care about validation as much as speed: we test our models against real data and are upfront about what they can and can’t do.

Find fields on the map, draw a section,: Find fields on the map, draw a section, and save the crop areas you want to keep.
Select Move map (the hand icon), then dr: Select Move map (the hand icon), then drag to your area. Scroll or pinch to zoom, or click a numbered cluster to zoom into that group.
Keep zooming until you see individual fi: Keep zooming until you see individual field dots. Hover over a dot to see its name and approximate area. The drawing tools become available once the dots have loaded.
The map pans, then a numbered cluster op: The map pans, then a numbered cluster opens to reveal individual field dots.
Choose Lasso selection. Press and drag a: Choose Lasso selection. Press and drag around the field dots you want, then release to close the outline and create a draft section.
In Lasso mode, click an individual field: In Lasso mode, click an individual field dot to toggle its selection. Press Esc to abandon an unfinished outline and return to Move map.
The lasso traces around three field dots: The lasso traces around three field dots and an Add button appears inside the section.
For a straight-sided outline, choose Poi: For a straight-sided outline, choose Point selection. Click at least three corners around the field dots you want, then click the first corner again to close the shape.
On a keyboard, press Backspace to undo t: On a keyboard, press Backspace to undo the last point, Enter to close the outline, or Esc to abandon it.
The cursor places four corners, then ret: The cursor places four corners, then returns to the first corner to close the section.
Click Add inside the outline to open Sec: Click Add inside the outline to open Section overview. Check the selected field count and approximate area, then click Analyze.
Wait for the map to find field boundarie: Wait for the map to find field boundaries and classify crops. If you drew the wrong section, use Cancel section and draw it again.
Add opens the section panel. Analyze sta: Add opens the section panel. Analyze starts a progress bar and the map reveals the predicted crop areas.
Click a crop icon on the map to include: Click a crop icon on the map to include or exclude that area. Use the checkbox next to a crop in Section overview to select or clear all areas of that crop.
Check the selected area count, then clic: Check the selected area count, then click Add areas to save your selection. The section closes once the save succeeds.
A map icon and a crop checkbox change wh: A map icon and a crop checkbox change which areas are selected before Add areas saves the remaining selection.
Why does the map look different from the: Why does the map look different from the crop prediction?
The satellite basemap comes from an imag: The satellite basemap comes from an imagery provider and may show an older capture. FieldSense uses newer available Sentinel-2 observations to predict what is growing. A different crop, harvest, or change to the field can therefore appear in the prediction before it appears on the basemap.
Why are the drawing tools disabled?: Why are the drawing tools disabled?
The lasso and point tools need individua: The lasso and point tools need individual field dots to be visible. Click a numbered cluster or zoom in, then wait for the field dots to load.
What is the difference between Add and A: What is the difference between Add and Add areas?
Add opens the draft section so you can r: Add opens the draft section so you can review and analyze it. Add areas saves the crop areas you kept after analysis. Cancel section discards the draft.
Why were some fields skipped during anal: Why were some fields skipped during analysis?
The tool needs a usable field boundary a: The tool needs a usable field boundary and enough clear satellite observations to classify a crop. If areas are skipped, review the remaining results or retry with a smaller section around the fields you need.
